newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin to sell first commercial paper deal.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin to sell first commercial paper deal.

text.p: The Wisconsin Building Commission on Thursday gave the green light to the state's first sale of tax-exempt commercial paper.
Frank Hoadley, the state's capital finance director, said the commission approved a $99.2 million general obligation deal that will mark the first in a $300 million commercial paper program.
He said the deal, secured by a liquidity facility from Bank of Nova Scotia and Commerz Bank AG, will probably be initially offered around April 3.
Goldman Sachs & Co. is the dealer for the issue and Merrill Lynch & Co. is the co-dealer, he added.
The program will enable the state to save money during the construction phase of state projects by borrowing lower on the yield curve, Hoadley said.
The state plans to replace the commercial paper with long-term GO bonds sometime between one and a half and two and a half years, he added.

The building commission is also considering a commercial paper program for transportation projects that could come up for approval at its meeting next month, Hoadley said. That program could total more than $160 million of debt.
